title: The role of intra-abdominal pressure and point of care ultrasound to guide decongestive therapy in Heart Failure (ABDOPOCUS-HF)
official: Utility of intra-abdominal pressure and clinical ultrasound for guiding diuretic treatment in patients with acute heart failure
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the complete resolution of congestion (ADVOR scale) after the first 72 hours of intravenous diuretic treatment on the hospital ward, between the standard treatment group and the intervention group (intra-abdominal pressure and ultrasound)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Men or women over 18 years of age
2. Diagnosis of HF based on the latest HF guidelines published in 2022
3. NT-proBNP > 1000 pg/mL or BNP > 250 pg/mL
4. Bladder catheterization in order to perform intra-abdominal pressure measurement
5. Intravascular or mixed pattern of congestion, defined as the presence of one or more clinical signs of congestion (edema, ascites and/or pleural effusion)
6. Signature of the informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patient with stay in the internal medicine department > 24 hours
2. Systolic blood pressure at admission < 100 mmHg
3. Heart rate at admission > 170 beats per minute (bpm)
4. Cardiogenic shock
5. Acute myocardial ischemia
6. Patients receiving renal replacement therapy (ultrafiltration or peritoneal dialysis).
7. Patients whose origin is the Intensive Care Unit
8. Renal transplant recipients
9. Serum hemoglobin < 9 g/dL
10. Pregnancy or lactation
11. Previous history of hypersensitivity to hydrochlorothiazide or furosemide.
12. Patients with recent cardiac surgery (last year) or cardiac transplant recipients
13. Need for inotropic support to maintain adequate cardiac and/or renal output
14. Absence of sufficient clinical congestion (ADVOR score = 0 at the time of randomization)
15. Patient refusal to participate in the clinical trial
16. Inability or contraindication to bladder catheterization
